mcqs.stem: Best guess: which law governs a contract to sell a used forklift?

choices.explanation: Common law governs services and real estate.
Correct. A forklift is a good.

mcqs.explanation: Sales of goods (movable tangible property) are governed by UCC Article 2.

mcqs.stem: A merchant signs a written offer stating it will remain open for 30 days, with no consideration. Can the merchant revoke it after 10 days?

choices.text: Yes, because the offer isn't supported by consideration
choices.explanation: A UCC firm offer needs no consideration.

choices.text: No, because all written offers are irrevocable
choices.explanation: Only firm offers or options are.

choices.text: Yes, if the goods cost more than $500
No; it's a firm offer, irrevocable for the stated period
choices.explanation: Correct. UCC 2-205: a merchant's signed written offer that states it will be held open is irrevocable for the stated time, not exceeding 3 months.

mcqs.explanation: UCC 2-205: a merchant's signed written offer that states it will be held open is irrevocable for the stated time, not exceeding 3 months.

mcqs.stem: A seller delivers nonconforming goods before the delivery deadline. The buyer rejects them. What right does the seller have?

choices.text: To cure with conforming goods within the contract period
choices.explanation: Correct. UCC 2-508: the seller may cure if the time for performance hasn't expired.

choices.text: None, because the buyer's rejection ends the contract
To force the buyer to keep the goods at a discount
choices.explanation: The buyer can't be forced to accept.

choices.text: To sue for the full price immediately

mcqs.explanation: UCC 2-508: the seller may cure if the time for performance hasn't expired.

mcqs.stem: An offeree mails an acceptance on May 1; the offeror mails a revocation on April 30 that arrives May 3. Is there a contract?

choices.text: No, because the revocation was sent first
choices.explanation: Revocations are effective on receipt; acceptances on dispatch.

choices.text: No, because acceptances are effective only on receipt
choices.explanation: The mailbox rule makes them effective on dispatch.

choices.text: Yes; the acceptance took effect when mailed on May 1
choices.explanation: Correct. Mailbox rule: acceptance is effective on dispatch (if properly sent); revocation is effective on receipt.

choices.text: Only if the offer was for the sale of goods

mcqs.explanation: Mailbox rule: acceptance is effective on dispatch (if properly sent); revocation is effective on receipt.

mcqs.stem: Which contract must be in writing under the statute of frauds?

choices.text: An oral agreement to paint a house in two weeks for $4,000
A promise to pay one's own debt
An employment contract for six months
An agreement to sell goods for $600

mcqs.explanation: MY LEGS: goods of $500 or more require a writing.

mcqs.stem: A contractor promises to finish a job on time but later demands extra pay to finish, which the owner promises. Is the promise enforceable under common law?

choices.text: No; a preexisting duty isn't new consideration
choices.explanation: Correct. Preexisting duty rule: performing an existing obligation isn't consideration for a new promise (common law).

choices.text: Yes, because the owner freely agreed to pay more
Yes, under the UCC's modification rule
choices.explanation: Construction is a service, governed by common law.

choices.text: Only if the new promise was made in writing
choices.explanation: A writing doesn't cure lack of consideration.

mcqs.explanation: Preexisting duty rule: performing an existing obligation isn't consideration for a new promise (common law).

mcqs.stem: A 16-year-old buys a gaming laptop and later wants to return it. What is the likely result?

choices.text: The minor is bound, because the laptop was delivered
The contract is void from the start
The minor may disaffirm the contract
choices.explanation: Correct. Contracts with minors are voidable at the minor's option (liability for necessaries is limited to reasonable value).
The minor holds the right to disaffirm.

mcqs.explanation: Contracts with minors are voidable at the minor's option (liability for necessaries is limited to reasonable value).

mcqs.stem: Under the parol evidence rule, which evidence may be admitted to vary a fully integrated written contract?

choices.text: An oral agreement made before signing that adds a price discount
choices.explanation: Prior agreements that contradict the writing are barred.

choices.text: A contemporaneous oral agreement changing the delivery date
Evidence that the contract was induced by fraud
choices.explanation: Correct. Exceptions: fraud, duress, mistake, subsequent modifications, and clarifying ambiguity.

mcqs.explanation: Exceptions: fraud, duress, mistake, subsequent modifications, and clarifying ambiguity.

mcqs.stem: A contract calls for $50,000 of liquidated damages for late completion; actual losses were hard to estimate and the amount was reasonable. Is it enforceable?

choices.text: No — liquidated damages are never enforced
No — punitive damages are required instead
choices.explanation: Punitive damages aren't available for breach.

choices.text: Only if actual damages are proven
choices.explanation: Proof of actual damages isn't required.

choices.text: Yes — it's a reasonable estimate, not a penalty
choices.explanation: Correct. Liquidated damages are enforceable when damages were hard to estimate and the amount is reasonable.

mcqs.explanation: Liquidated damages are enforceable when damages were hard to estimate and the amount is reasonable.

mcqs.stem: A merchant seller ships goods FOB shipping point by common carrier; the goods are destroyed in transit. Who bears the loss?

choices.explanation: Risk passed at delivery to the carrier.
Correct. FOB shipping point: risk passes to the buyer when goods are delivered to the carrier.
The carrier may be liable, but between buyer and seller the buyer bears risk.
The UCC assigns risk to one party.

mcqs.explanation: FOB shipping point: risk passes to the buyer when goods are delivered to the carrier.

mcqs.stem: Which statement about the implied warranty of merchantability is correct?

choices.text: It arises in every sale of goods, by any seller
choices.explanation: Only when the seller is a merchant for those goods.

choices.text: It arises only when the seller is a merchant in such goods
choices.explanation: Correct. UCC 2-314: merchantability is implied only for merchant sellers.

choices.text: It can't be disclaimed by the seller
choices.explanation: It can be disclaimed (e.g., "as is" or conspicuous language mentioning merchantability).

choices.text: It requires a written statement by the seller

mcqs.explanation: UCC 2-314: merchantability is implied only for merchant sellers.

mcqs.stem: A party repudiates a contract before performance is due. What may the other party do?

choices.text: Nothing until the performance date arrives
Treat it as breach now, or wait a reasonable time
choices.explanation: Correct. Anticipatory repudiation allows an immediate suit or waiting for performance.

choices.text: Collect punitive damages from the repudiating party
choices.explanation: Punitive damages aren't available for breach.

choices.text: Force specific performance in all cases

mcqs.explanation: Anticipatory repudiation allows an immediate suit or waiting for performance.

mcqs.stem: Which contract is most likely to be subject to specific performance?

choices.text: A contract to sell a unique parcel of land
choices.explanation: Correct. Specific performance applies when money damages are inadequate — land and unique goods.

choices.text: A contract to sell 100 generic widgets at list price
A loan agreement with a bank

mcqs.explanation: Specific performance applies when money damages are inadequate — land and unique goods.

mcqs.stem: A buyer agrees to purchase a building from a seller. With the seller's consent, a third party takes the buyer's place, and the seller expressly releases the original buyer. What is this?

choices.explanation: In an assignment or delegation the original party remains liable unless released.
Correct. A novation substitutes a new party with the consent of all and releases the original party.
An accord substitutes a different performance, not a new party.
Rescission cancels the contract; here it continues with a new party.

mcqs.explanation: Novation: new party, everyone consents, original party released.

mcqs.stem: Between merchants, a buyer's acceptance adds a term disclaiming all warranties. The seller doesn't object. What is the result under the UCC?

choices.text: A contract forms without the new term
choices.explanation: Correct. A term that materially alters the offer isn't included.
The UCC rejects the mirror-image rule.

choices.text: A contract forms with the new term

mcqs.explanation: UCC 2-207: additional terms in a merchant's acceptance become part of the contract unless they materially alter it, the offer limits acceptance, or there's an objection.

mcqs.stem: A merchant's signed, written promise to keep an offer open is irrevocable without consideration for up to:
mcqs.explanation: UCC 2-205: a merchant's signed written firm offer is irrevocable for the time stated, up to 3 months.

mcqs.stem: After an employee retires, her employer promises her $10,000 for her past years of service. Is the promise enforceable?

choices.explanation: Correct. Past consideration isn't bargained for.

mcqs.explanation: Past consideration isn't valid consideration because it wasn't bargained for in exchange for the promise.

mcqs.stem: A contractor's bid omits a $40,000 item by error. The owner had no reason to know of the mistake and accepts. Is the contract enforceable?

choices.text: No, any mistake voids the contract
No, because the error was material
Only at the corrected bid price

choices.explanation: Correct. The owner didn't know of the error.

mcqs.explanation: A unilateral mistake generally doesn't allow avoidance unless the other party knew or should have known of it.

mcqs.stem: A buyer responds to an offer by proposing a lower price. What happens to the original offer?

choices.explanation: Correct. A counteroffer rejects the offer.

mcqs.explanation: Under common law, a counteroffer operates as a rejection and terminates the original offer.

mcqs.stem: Between merchants, a seller sends a signed written confirmation of an oral $8,000 sale. The buyer doesn't object within 10 days. What is the effect?

choices.text: No contract exists without the buyer's signature
The statute of frauds is satisfied
choices.explanation: Correct. The merchant confirmation rule applies.

choices.text: The buyer may still avoid it freely

mcqs.explanation: UCC 2-201(2): between merchants, a written confirmation binds the recipient unless written objection is given within 10 days.

mcqs.stem: A debtor in a good-faith dispute sends a check marked 'payment in full' for less than the amount claimed, and the creditor cashes it. What is the effect?

choices.text: The creditor can sue for the balance

mcqs.explanation: Cashing a full-payment check for a disputed (unliquidated) debt creates an accord and satisfaction.

mcqs.stem: A city contracts to build a park next to a store, which expects more customers. The city breaches. Can the store sue?

choices.explanation: Correct. Only intended beneficiaries may sue.
The contract wasn't for its benefit.
No debt was owed to it.

mcqs.explanation: Incidental beneficiaries can't enforce a contract; intended beneficiaries can.

mcqs.stem: A contract to sell a specific painting is signed, but the painting is destroyed by fire before delivery through no one's fault. What is the effect?

choices.text: The seller must find a substitute

mcqs.explanation: Destruction of the specific subject matter without fault makes performance objectively impossible and discharges the contract.

mcqs.stem: A store's newspaper ad says: "First 3 customers Saturday at 9 a.m. get a $1,000 TV for $10." A customer arrives first. Is there a contract?

choices.text: Yes, the specific ad is an offer
choices.explanation: Correct. Definite terms and a limited number make it an offer.

choices.text: Only if the store agrees later

mcqs.explanation: Most ads are invitations, but a specific ad that leaves nothing open for negotiation can be an offer.

mcqs.stem: A seller writes: "If I don't hear from you by Friday, we have a deal." The buyer says nothing. Is there a contract?

choices.explanation: Correct. Absent prior dealings, silence doesn't accept.

choices.text: Only if the price was fair

mcqs.explanation: An offeror can't impose acceptance by silence absent a prior course of dealing or a duty to speak.

mcqs.stem: An offeror mails a revocation on May 1, received May 4. The offeree mails an acceptance on May 3. Is there a contract?

choices.explanation: Correct. Revocation is effective on receipt.

choices.text: Only if it arrived by May 4

mcqs.explanation: Under the mailbox rule, acceptance is effective on dispatch; revocation is effective on receipt.

mcqs.stem: An uncle promises his niece $20,000 to buy a car. In reliance, she buys one with a loan. He refuses to pay. What may she rely on?

choices.explanation: No benefit was conferred on him.
Correct. Reasonable, detrimental reliance can enforce a gratuitous promise.

mcqs.explanation: Promissory estoppel enforces promises that induce foreseeable, detrimental reliance.

mcqs.stem: Merchants agree in good faith to raise the price of goods under an existing sales contract, with no new consideration. Is the modification binding?

choices.explanation: Correct. UCC modifications need no consideration.
That isn't what the rule says.

mcqs.explanation: UCC 2-209: a good-faith modification of a sales contract needs no consideration.

mcqs.stem: A famous painter contracted to paint a portrait assigns the contract to another painter. May she?

choices.explanation: Correct. Personal services contracts aren't assignable without consent.

choices.text: Yes, if the assignee is skilled

mcqs.explanation: Duties requiring personal skill or judgment can't be delegated or assigned without consent.

mcqs.stem: A contractor delegates a paving job to another qualified contractor, who does poor work. Is the original contractor liable?

choices.explanation: Correct. Delegation doesn't release the original obligor.

choices.text: Only if it was a novation

mcqs.explanation: A delegating party stays liable unless the other party agrees to a novation.

mcqs.stem: A buyer wrongfully cancels a $50,000 purchase. The seller could resell the goods for $48,000 but refuses to try. What may the seller recover?
mcqs.explanation: A nonbreaching party can't recover damages it could have avoided with reasonable efforts.

mcqs.stem: A seller delivers nonconforming goods before the delivery deadline. The buyer rejects them. What may the seller do?

choices.explanation: Correct. The UCC allows cure within the contract time.

choices.text: Demand payment for the goods sent

mcqs.explanation: UCC 2-508: if time remains, a seller may notify the buyer and cure with a conforming delivery.

mcqs.stem: A merchant seller agrees that the buyer will pick up goods at the seller's store. Before pickup, the goods are destroyed by fire. Who bears the loss?

choices.explanation: Correct. Risk passes from a merchant seller on the buyer's receipt.
That isn't what the rule says.

mcqs.explanation: When no carrier is used, risk passes on the buyer's receipt if the seller is a merchant.

mcqs.stem: Under the UCC statute of frauds, a contract for the sale of goods must be in writing at what price?
mcqs.explanation: Contracts for the sale of goods for $500 or more generally need a signed writing.

mcqs.stem: Under the mailbox rule, when is an acceptance sent by an authorized means effective?

choices.explanation: Correct. Acceptance is effective on dispatch.

mcqs.explanation: An acceptance by an authorized method is effective when sent.

mcqs.stem: What is the status of a contract made by a minor?

choices.explanation: Correct. Only the minor may disaffirm.

mcqs.explanation: A minor's contract is voidable at the minor's option; the adult is bound.

mcqs.stem: Under the UCC, a merchant buyer accepts an offer but adds a term requiring the seller to pay freight — a material change. What is the result?

choices.explanation: Under the UCC, a contract forms.

choices.text: A contract forms, including the freight term
choices.explanation: Material terms don't automatically become part.

choices.text: A contract forms without the material new term
choices.explanation: Correct. UCC 2-207: between merchants, additional terms become part unless material, objected to, or the offer limits acceptance.

choices.text: The acceptance is a counteroffer under the mirror-image rule

mcqs.explanation: UCC 2-207: between merchants, additional terms become part unless material, objected to, or the offer limits acceptance.

mcqs.stem: Which is valid consideration?

choices.text: A promise to pay for work already completed
A promise to make a gift to a relative
A promise to perform an existing contractual duty
A promise not to sue on a good-faith claim
choices.explanation: Correct. Forbearance from a good-faith legal claim is a bargained-for legal detriment.

mcqs.explanation: Forbearance from a good-faith legal claim is a bargained-for legal detriment.

mcqs.stem: An offer to sell land is sent May 1. The offeree replies May 3: "I accept, but the price must be $5,000 lower." What is the effect?

choices.text: A contract at the original price
A contract at the lower price
A valid acceptance with a proposal
choices.explanation: That's the UCC approach for goods.

mcqs.explanation: Land is governed by common law; a changed term is a counteroffer.

mcqs.stem: Which remedy is generally unavailable for breach of contract?

choices.explanation: Compensatory damages are the standard remedy.
Correct. Not available for breach alone.

mcqs.explanation: Punitive damages require a tort such as fraud.

mcqs.stem: Under the UCC statute of frauds, which contract must be evidenced by a writing to be enforceable?

choices.text: A contract for services to finish in six months
choices.explanation: Contracts performable within a year needn't be written.

choices.text: A contract for the sale of goods for $800
choices.explanation: Correct. Sales of goods for $500 or more require a writing.

choices.text: A contract to sell goods for $300
An oral promise to pay one's own debt
choices.explanation: Promises to pay one's own debt aren't covered.

mcqs.explanation: UCC 2-201: a contract for the sale of goods for $500 or more requires a signed writing, subject to exceptions.

mcqs.stem: A merchant makes a signed written offer to sell goods, stating it will remain open for 60 days. No consideration is given. The offer is:

choices.text: Revocable at any time before acceptance
choices.explanation: Firm offers by merchants can't be revoked.

choices.text: Irrevocable only if the buyer pays for the option
choices.explanation: A firm offer needs no consideration.
Correct. A merchant's firm offer is irrevocable for the stated period, up to three months.
The maximum without consideration is three months.

mcqs.explanation: UCC 2-205: a merchant's signed written firm offer is irrevocable without consideration for the time stated, not exceeding three months.

mcqs.stem: After an employee retires, the employer promises to pay her $5,000 for her past years of loyal service. The promise is:

choices.text: Enforceable, because the service had value

choices.explanation: The UCC governs goods, not services.
Correct. Something already done can't be bargained for.

mcqs.explanation: Consideration must be bargained for; past consideration doesn't support a new promise.

mcqs.stem: Two merchants exchange forms. The buyer's acceptance adds a minor term that doesn't materially alter the offer; the seller doesn't object. Under UCC 2-207, the added term:

choices.explanation: Correct. Between merchants, nonmaterial additional terms become part unless the offer limits acceptance or an objection is made.

choices.text: Is a counteroffer that prevents a contract
choices.explanation: Under the UCC a definite acceptance forms a contract.

choices.text: Is ignored because all terms must match
choices.explanation: The mirror-image rule doesn't apply to goods.

mcqs.explanation: UCC 2-207: additional terms between merchants become part of the contract unless they materially alter it, the offer expressly limits acceptance, or timely objection is given.

flashcards.back: Marriage, >1 Year, Land, Executor, Goods ≥ $500, Suretyship.
A merchant's signed written offer; irrevocable for the stated time, up to 3 months, without consideration.
Acceptance is effective on dispatch; revocation on receipt.
Not consideration under common law; UCC modifications need no consideration.

flashcards.front: Risk of loss — FOB shipping point vs. destination
flashcards.back: Shipping point: on delivery to the carrier. Destination: on tender at the destination.
Only when the seller is a merchant in those goods; disclaimable.
